## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-xcgm-r5h9-7989)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/14b6ee851fb16ec199acb950de0c82d476799e7d)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/bf88077ebb14f4c29924b8e8904cba20c55c28b8)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-2fqr-mr3j-6wp8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a329a7aacad5284f087af36103aff778746da0f2)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4m7w-qmgq-4wj5)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ca2b6c28a25726527a8b60f25960262a91ed0e0)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hw-fmq6-xxg2)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/5ab61bb4cd88f19b712f12c7c9295fe262bf804d)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3cq-j2xw-wf74)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/4f7480e474cccc6a8cc2c92ad3f17a31dedf8232)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-9x8q-7h8h-wcw9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a762eda5242f6490d6ba667533193f8b473ad587)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling through the handling of HTTP/1 pipelined requests queue without a limit. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4fvr-rgm6-gqmc)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dfdfa9d5aad5d21f91c79fb2ceeba0f8046cb6cf)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the `llhttp` component. An attacker can manipulate HTTP response headers by injecting null bytes or control characters, causing headers to be interpreted differently by various components, which may lead to security bypass or inconsistent behavior between the application and reverse proxies.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hf-3vf5-4wqf)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/9370b9714a7a56003cacd31a9b4ae16eab109ba4)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via the `reason` parameter in the HTTP response creation process. An attacker can inject unauthorized headers or manipulate the HTTP response by supplying specially crafted input containing carriage return characters.

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the processing of multipart headers. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending a response with an unusually large number of multipart headers.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Request Smuggling via the processing of duplicate `Host` headers. An attacker can bypass security checks enforced by a reverse proxy by sending requests with multiple `Host` headers, potentially causing the proxy and the backend to interpret different host values and allowing unauthorized access to privileged sub-applications.

**Note:**

This is only exploitable if a reverse proxy applies security rules based on the `Host` header and the backend uses domain-based routing.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-c427-h43c-vf67)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/53e2e6fc58b89c6185be7820bd2c9f40216b3000)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/e00ca3cca92c465c7913c4beb763a72da9ed8349)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `Request.post` function. An attacker can cause excessive memory allocation by sending a specially crafted multipart request containing large non-file fields.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/cbb774f38330563422ca0c413a71021d7b944145)

vulnerabilities.title: Information Exposure
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Exposure in the handling of cross-origin redirects, where `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` headers are not properly removed. An attacker can obtain sensitive information by causing a user to follow a redirect to a malicious origin.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-966j-vmvw-g2g9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/5351c980dcec7ad385730efdf4e1f4338b24fdb6)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the construction of multipart request headers when untrusted input is used for the `content_type` parameter. An attacker can inject arbitrary headers or manipulate HTTP requests by supplying specially crafted values.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-2vrm-gr82-f7m5)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/9a6ada97e2c6cf1ce31727c6c9fcea17c21f6f06)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `TCPConnector` function. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by making requests to a very large number of hosts, leading to resource exhaustion.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hcc4-c3v8-rx92)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/c4d77c3533122be353b8afca8e8675e3b4cbda98)

vulnerabilities.title: Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) in the static resource handler on Windows. An attacker can extract NTLMv2 credential hashes by accessing specially crafted remote paths, potentially leading to credential theft.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-p998-jp59-783m)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ae2aa076c84573df83fc1fdc39eec0f5862fe3d)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling due to insufficient restrictions in the handling of HTTP headers and trailers. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending specially crafted requests, potentially leading to service unavailability.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0c2e9da51126238a421568eb7c5b53e5b5d17b36)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Request Smuggling via the processing of duplicate `Host` headers. An attacker can bypass security checks enforced by a reverse proxy by sending requests with multiple `Host` headers, potentially causing the proxy and the backend to interpret different host values and allowing unauthorized access to privileged sub-applications.

**Note:**

This is only exploitable if a reverse proxy applies security rules based on the `Host` header and the backend uses domain-based routing.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4m7w-qmgq-4wj5)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hw-fmq6-xxg2)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3cq-j2xw-wf74)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-9x8q-7h8h-wcw9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a762eda5242f6490d6ba667533193f8b473ad587)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling through the handling of HTTP/1 pipelined requests queue without a limit. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the `llhttp` component. An attacker can manipulate HTTP response headers by injecting null bytes or control characters, causing headers to be interpreted differently by various components, which may lead to security bypass or inconsistent behavior between the application and reverse proxies.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-xcgm-r5h9-7989)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/14b6ee851fb16ec199acb950de0c82d476799e7d)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/bf88077ebb14f4c29924b8e8904cba20c55c28b8)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-2fqr-mr3j-6wp8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a329a7aacad5284f087af36103aff778746da0f2)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4m7w-qmgq-4wj5)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ca2b6c28a25726527a8b60f25960262a91ed0e0)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hw-fmq6-xxg2)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/5ab61bb4cd88f19b712f12c7c9295fe262bf804d)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3cq-j2xw-wf74)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/4f7480e474cccc6a8cc2c92ad3f17a31dedf8232)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-9x8q-7h8h-wcw9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a762eda5242f6490d6ba667533193f8b473ad587)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling through the handling of HTTP/1 pipelined requests queue without a limit. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4fvr-rgm6-gqmc)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dfdfa9d5aad5d21f91c79fb2ceeba0f8046cb6cf)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the `llhttp` component. An attacker can manipulate HTTP response headers by injecting null bytes or control characters, causing headers to be interpreted differently by various components, which may lead to security bypass or inconsistent behavior between the application and reverse proxies.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hf-3vf5-4wqf)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/9370b9714a7a56003cacd31a9b4ae16eab109ba4)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Request Smuggling via the processing of duplicate `Host` headers. An attacker can bypass security checks enforced by a reverse proxy by sending requests with multiple `Host` headers, potentially causing the proxy and the backend to interpret different host values and allowing unauthorized access to privileged sub-applications.

**Note:**

This is only exploitable if a reverse proxy applies security rules based on the `Host` header and the backend uses domain-based routing.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-c427-h43c-vf67)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/53e2e6fc58b89c6185be7820bd2c9f40216b3000)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/e00ca3cca92c465c7913c4beb763a72da9ed8349)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `Request.post` function. An attacker can cause excessive memory allocation by sending a specially crafted multipart request containing large non-file fields.

## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Exposure in the handling of cross-origin redirects, where `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` headers are not properly removed. An attacker can obtain sensitive information by causing a user to follow a redirect to a malicious origin.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the construction of multipart request headers when untrusted input is used for the `content_type` parameter. An attacker can inject arbitrary headers or manipulate HTTP requests by supplying specially crafted values.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `TCPConnector` function. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by making requests to a very large number of hosts, leading to resource exhaustion.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) in the static resource handler on Windows. An attacker can extract NTLMv2 credential hashes by accessing specially crafted remote paths, potentially leading to credential theft.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling due to insufficient restrictions in the handling of HTTP headers and trailers. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending specially crafted requests, potentially leading to service unavailability.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4m7w-qmgq-4wj5)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hw-fmq6-xxg2)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3cq-j2xw-wf74)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/4f7480e474cccc6a8cc2c92ad3f17a31dedf8232)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-9x8q-7h8h-wcw9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a762eda5242f6490d6ba667533193f8b473ad587)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling through the handling of HTTP/1 pipelined requests queue without a limit. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References

## Overview

An attacker can manipulate HTTP response headers by injecting null bytes or control characters, causing headers to be interpreted differently by various components, which may lead to security bypass or inconsistent behavior between the application and reverse proxies.
## Remediation

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-xcgm-r5h9-7989)

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.

- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:

An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.

vulnerabilities.description:

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/f54c40851b0d6c4bbdab97ba518a223adda32478)
vulnerabilities.name: aiohttp

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling via the `websocket` checks. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending large incomplete frame payloads, potentially leading to service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-xcgm-r5h9-7989)

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2491474)

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Response Splitting
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-m6qw-4cw2-hm4m)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/bf88077ebb14f4c29924b8e8904cba20c55c28b8)

vulnerabilities.title: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-2fqr-mr3j-6wp8)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4m7w-qmgq-4wj5)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0ca2b6c28a25726527a8b60f25960262a91ed0e0)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hw-fmq6-xxg2)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/5ab61bb4cd88f19b712f12c7c9295fe262bf804d)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3cq-j2xw-wf74)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/4f7480e474cccc6a8cc2c92ad3f17a31dedf8232)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Resource Shutdown or Release
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-9x8q-7h8h-wcw9)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/a762eda5242f6490d6ba667533193f8b473ad587)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling through the handling of HTTP/1 pipelined requests queue without a limit. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a large number of pipelined requests, potentially causing service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-4fvr-rgm6-gqmc)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the `llhttp` component. An attacker can manipulate HTTP response headers by injecting null bytes or control characters, causing headers to be interpreted differently by various components, which may lead to security bypass or inconsistent behavior between the application and reverse proxies.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-63hf-3vf5-4wqf)

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via the `reason` parameter in the HTTP response creation process. An attacker can inject unauthorized headers or manipulate the HTTP response by supplying specially crafted input containing carriage return characters.

vulnerabilities.description:

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the processing of multipart headers. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending a response with an unusually large number of multipart headers.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: HTTP Request Smuggling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Request Smuggling via the processing of duplicate `Host` headers. An attacker can bypass security checks enforced by a reverse proxy by sending requests with multiple `Host` headers, potentially causing the proxy and the backend to interpret different host values and allowing unauthorized access to privileged sub-applications.

**Note:**

This is only exploitable if a reverse proxy applies security rules based on the `Host` header and the backend uses domain-based routing.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-c427-h43c-vf67)

vulnerabilities.description:

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `Request.post` function. An attacker can cause excessive memory allocation by sending a specially crafted multipart request containing large non-file fields.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Information Exposure in the handling of cross-origin redirects, where `Cookie` and `Proxy-Authorization` headers are not properly removed. An attacker can obtain sensitive information by causing a user to follow a redirect to a malicious origin.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting in the construction of multipart request headers when untrusted input is used for the `content_type` parameter. An attacker can inject arbitrary headers or manipulate HTTP requests by supplying specially crafted values.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)

vulnerabilities.title: Origin Validation Error
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error via the `cookies` parameter, which is processed by `_connect_and_send_request()` in `client.py`. An attacker who can control a redirect on a request that passes `cookies` on a per-request basis can expose data from those requests.

## Workaround 
This vulnerability can be mitigated by using a `Cookie` header in the `headers` parameter instead of the `cookies` parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hg6j-4rv6-33pg)

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insufficiently Protected Credentials via the `DigestAuthMiddleware` class when authentication responses are sent after following cross-origin redirects. An attacker can obtain authentication digests by leveraging an open redirect or similar issue to redirect a client to an attacker-controlled domain.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if the client follows redirects to attacker-controlled domains.

## Workaround 

This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling the `follow_redirects` option.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-hpj7-wq8m-9hgp)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/38d16060037e1bfcd6d677abababa3c2a4bb58fa)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to HTTP Response Splitting via `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers` when attacker-controlled input is included in multipart or payload headers. An attacker can inject additional headers or alter the contents of a request by supplying specially crafted input.

**Note:** This is only exploitable if user-controlled strings are passed into the `headers` parameter of `MultipartWriter.append` or `Payload.headers`.

Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor in the `CookieJar.save` and `CookieJar.load` functions. An attacker can cause cookies intended for a specific host to be sent to subdomains by persisting and restoring cookies, potentially leading to unintended information disclosure.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Validation of Certificate with Host Mismatch in the `server_hostname` parameter handling during HTTPS connection reuse. An attacker can bypass intended TLS SNI checks by reusing an existing connection with a different `server_hostname`, potentially allowing connections to unintended hosts.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `C HTTP parser` when the `max_line_size` check is bypassed for fragmented lines. An attacker can cause excessive memory consumption by sending oversized HTTP request lines, potentially resulting in resource exhaustion and service disruption.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) during cleanup. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted compressed payload that is decompressed into memory in a single chunk.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.1 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Resource Shutdown or Release in the payload response resources when a client disconnects during a write operation. An attacker can cause temporary resource exhaustion by repeatedly initiating connections and disconnecting mid-transfer, leading to open files or similar resources not being released until garbage collection occurs.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling due to insufficient restrictions in the handling of HTTP headers and trailers. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending specially crafted requests, potentially leading to service unavailability.
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.13.4 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-w2fm-2cpv-w7v5)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/0c2e9da51126238a421568eb7c5b53e5b5d17b36)
- [GitHub Release](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/releases/tag/v3.13.4)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2454093)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `CookieJar.load()` function. A user who convinces another user to load a malicious serialized object can cause the execution of arbitrary code.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `aiohttp` to version 3.14.0 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/security/advisories/GHSA-jg22-mg44-37j8)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/aio-libs/aiohttp/commit/dcf40f30637e8752c76781cf6703b5a236749a00)
